_why: FOUNDATION1e part 1 (the foundation design §3.1's census sentence, D212): the one list of the sites where a path decides today how a line goes on. `CourseCensusTests` holds it exactly: a source file of the driver, host, modules or app with a shape below that neither reads the course nor is named here fails, a count that differs fails, a named file that is gone or whose shape is gone fails, and `floor` is the least number of file and shape pairs found. Every site is `not yet moved`, its `row` the Part B row that adopts it (h for conversations, i for driven lines, as §10 lists them). `hands` is true where the site's own body opens a part and hands it words: row d-ii's later parts read it for every site that opens and hands words, and a caller or a planner that only chooses is false. `moving`, on each such site alone (FOUNDATION1d-ii part 4), says how its open moves the words: `moves`, through the keyed door, its delivery read from the destination's moved words, the driven carry-on and the refused open among them (part 5); `unkeyed`, the hand-over and the curve, until rows f-v and h; `no move`, words handed to its own record or a fresh one, with no record left, the driven go-on's own resume among them. `box` names the ended limit move's members that read the destination's moved words, until row f-vi retires the box. `records` names each member whose move keeps its move record in the store, deciding it through the conversations' holder, with the row that adopted it (FOUNDATION1f-ii part a: the live limit move; FOUNDATION1f-iv part a: the driven carry-on); rows f-iii, f-v and f-vi add theirs. `paths` are the survey's paths A to N (the foundation survey §2.2). Paths L and M are not course decisions and are named so in `notDecisions`.

sites.what: the driven look's go-on of a record the planner chose, which falls back to a new part
the go-on's resume and the limit resume's step 1, each asking the account rule
the new part's `from`, in order hand-over, limit, curve, retry, carry-on
the driven look's answers-alone hold before a go-on
the driven go-on: the judge, the resume and the words taken off
a quest's hand-over: the person's ask and the agent's, with the consent before the ask, the move taken from the store (f-v part c)
the page's and the terminal's hand-over press on a quest's session, deciding its driven move (f-v part c)
the driven limit resume: which record, its word keyed by the cool-off
a record ended past its transient bound
the planner's go-on, carry-on, limited carry-on and transient hold
the planner's reading of a record ended past its transient bound
the supervisor's door refusing a decision while the line stands at the bound
the replacement of a conversation whose model the account did not offer
a workflow's send-back and a go-on with findings: a word the dispatcher owns, an ended chat going on as path B

adapted.why: The runner's briefed press, lost go-on and closed quest's cooling go-on hand to moves that decide through the course; the runner names no course type.
The runner's doors for start-from, start-with, the briefed move and the lost go-on are adapters of the course's readers; the runner names no course type.

records.why: the live limit move: decided before its turns are held, each phase written before what it fences, each handed word's sent at the wire before its take, and delivered after it

the ended limit move: decided at old-ended before its keyed open, an ended record having no part to end, each later phase written as the live move's, and no limit-move box written beside it; a box an older build wrote is imported once at the come-up

the curve's move: decided where it is judged to move, taken through the hand-over's take with each phase written before what it fences and the prompt's outcome at the wire (its message carries no word id, so no word's sent), and no hand-over box written beside it

a conversation's hand-over, the person's press and the agent's ask: decided at the ask, kept at decided or quiescing until its turn ends, taken through the hand-over's own take with each phase written before what it fences, and no hand-over box written beside it; an older build's conversation box is imported once at the come-up

a quest's hand-over, the person's press and the agent's ask: decided at the ask as a driven move, taken by the driver's look (quiescing while its session runs, old-ended once stopped and the quest held), continued by the carry-on it starts, and no hand-over box written beside it; an older build's quest box is imported once by the driven take-up

the driven carry-on: decided at old-ended before its keyed open, or, for the carry-on a quest's hand-over starts, the hand-over's own move gone on from (row f-v part c), each phase written before what it fences, each handed word's sent where the door's write of the first prompt returns, with the take after it (part b; part a wrote it where the take returned), and ended by its phase wherever the start stops

moved.why: A conversation's hand-over, the person's press and the agent's ask, decides through the course in HandOver.cs, its chat runner adapter in ChatHandOver.cs, so no site of it is left.
The live limit move decides through the course in LimitMove.cs; the runner's call of it is an adapter.
The ended limit move, the wake and the conversation's go-on decide through the course in LimitMove.cs, LimitWaits.cs and ChatGoOn.cs.
The briefed move decides through the course in BriefedMove.cs; the runner's doors to it are adapters.
Start-from and start-with decide through the course in ChatRunner.StartFrom.cs and StartWith.cs; go-on-new moved in branch 2.

notDecisions.why: A workflow's send-back is a word between turns that the dispatcher owns; an ended conversation's go-on from it is path B, with B's own-account rule.
SWITCHCTX1's carry is a move's `how`, not a decision; it has no code yet, so the census reserves it and fails the day a source writes a carried move.
